card: Replaces hard-coded numeric RPC error codes across functional and unit tests with named RPCErrorCode constants. This solves test readability and maintainability issues where developers must manually cross-reference error code numbers against protocol.h to understand expected test failures. The PR touches 126 test files, primarily driven by scripted diffs, with no changes to node behavior or external dependencies.
evidence: "When a test expects an RPC error by number, readers have to look up the code to tell which failure it covers." (PR description)
Author notes the change was split out while reviewing #36976; no production bugs or external user impact are claimed.
problem: Tests expecting RPC errors use raw numeric error codes (such as `-8` or `-26`). Developers reviewing test failures or writing tests must manually look up these numbers in `protocol.h` to determine which failure condition is being tested.

risk.why: A typo or mismatch in an error code constant would cause test assertions to check the wrong error code or fail CI, without affecting production binaries.

scope_notes: Touches 126 files (+1501/-1022) across the test suite, but two of the three commits are mechanical scripted diffs with verify scripts in the commit messages, and the PR description includes a sed script to validate that constants match original numeric values.
summary: Replaces hard-coded numeric RPC error codes across the functional and C++ unit test suites with named constants. It exports the C++ `RPCErrorCode` enum values from `src/rpc/protocol.h` to `test_framework/rpc_error_codes.py`, updates assertions in functional tests via scripted diffs, and converts C++ unit tests and test client error constants.
